summary: Nipissing District, Ontario tower: 1910 wooden original, 1961 100 ft steel tower, restored and reopened 1998; visitors climb it today.

facts.design: Aermotor LL-25 (Firelookout.ca tower type); the 1961 tower is described as 100-foot steel

staffing.status: no longer used to spot fires
staffing.as_of: undated; a visitor page says it was last used 25 years before that page was written

facts.agency: Ontario Ministry of Natural Resources (Forest Rangers), per the 1998 dedication

access.note: Visitors climb the tower today; a visitor page gives a $2 admission to the Caribou Mountain visitor area (undated)

visit.trail_note: Steps and a trail up Caribou Mountain; the municipality warns the steps can be icy in early spring or slippery when wet

events.note: Original square-timber tower, 45 ft, a few metres east of the present site
Late-1930s 85 ft steel tower demolished and sent over the cliff face because of rust; 100 ft steel tower erected the same year by seven Forest Rangers
Restored in the mid-1990s; reopened and dedicated 9 August 1998 (municipality says re-dedicated in 1998)

corrections.proposed: 1961 built (current steel tower); 1910 is the original wooden tower
corrections.why: The standing tower was erected in 1961. Sources date the wooden tower to 1910, and it was replaced.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The municipality says the tower was restored in the mid-1990s and re-dedicated in 1998. Visitor pages give the reopening as 9 August 1998. These fit together: restoration work in the mid-1990s, reopening in 1998.
Firelookout.ca leaves its structured height field as N/A, but its text describes a 100-foot steel tower, which Northern Ontario Travel also gives. The story uses 30.5 m.

notes_for_editor: Four sources agree on the 1910 wooden tower, the late-1930s 85 ft tower and the 1961 100 ft steel tower. The Aermotor LL-25 design appears only in the Firelookout.ca tower-type field; no narrative source names the maker, so the design is flagged here. The late-1930s replacement has no exact year, so it has no event row. The $2 admission comes from an undated visitor page; check fees before publishing. The only fire-use date is the undated 'last used 25 years' line, so no staffing end year is given. The geohub dataset page returned no text. No new photos. Record correction: the built event should be 1961 for the standing tower.
